books.title: The Death of Ivan Ilyich
books.author: Leo Tolstoy
books.subtitle: A novella
books.blurb:
Ivan Ilyich has everything society considers the marks of a successful life. When illness forces him to confront his mortality, he begins to question everything he once valued.

A short novella exploring suffering, death and the meaning of a life well lived.
books.reason: A short classic that invites thoughtful conversation about mortality, faith and the things we value most.

books.author_bio: Russian novelist and moral thinker, best known for War and Peace and Anna Karenina. In his later writing, he explored questions of faith, conscience, mortality and the meaning of life. The Death of Ivan Ilyich was published in 1886.

books.title: Surprised by Joy
books.author: C. S. Lewis
books.subtitle: The Shape of My Early Life
books.blurb:
C. S. Lewis recounts his childhood, education and early adulthood, tracing the elusive experience he called Joy and his gradual journey from atheism to Christian faith.

An autobiographical reflection on longing, imagination and belief.
books.reason: An exploration of longing, faith and the unexpected paths by which we come to believe.
books.author_bio: C. S. Lewis was a British writer, literary scholar and Christian apologist. Born in Belfast, he taught at Oxford and Cambridge and wrote both fiction and works exploring Christianity. Surprised by Joy, published in 1955, recounts his early life and conversion.

further_reading.title: The Great Divorce — C. S. Lewis

books.author: J. I. Packer
books.subtitle: Christian living
books.blurb: A Christian classic about knowing God and living in relationship with him.
books.reason: Example recommendation only; not an approved pastor recommendation.
books.author_bio: An English-born theologian and writer who spent much of his later career in Canada. His work emphasised the importance of knowing God through Scripture. Knowing God was first published in 1973.
